# Starter: course number resolution

This is a small, self-contained TypeScript project. It is **not** part of
the Berkeleytime monorepo -- it has its own `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`
and doesn't need anything else installed.

## Setup

```sh
npm install
npm test
```

`npm test` runs the test suite once (via vitest) and exits. Use
`npm run test:watch` if you'd like it to re-run on save while you work.

You should see the suite fail against the code as given -- every test
hits a "not implemented" error. That's the starting point, not a setup
problem.

## The scenario

Two related fixture "tables" live in `src/data.ts`:

- `courses` -- a catalog table. Each course has a `subject` + `number`
  (e.g. `INTEGBI 32`). This table is fed by an upstream system that
  renumbers courses on its own schedule, and it can lag: after a course is
  renumbered, this record keeps reporting the **old** number for a while.
- `classes` -- specific term offerings. Each one references a course by
  id, but also carries its own `subject` / `courseNumber`, which are
  always current. A `classes` row also has a `number` field, which is
  unrelated to the course number -- it's the section number (e.g. `"001"`).

`src/curatedClasses.ts` implements the admin "curate a class" feature:
an admin picks a class from a catalog picker (`buildCatalogOptions` /
`searchCatalog`), and the selection is saved (`curateClass`) and later
shown/searched on a list page (`searchCuratedClasses`).

## The task

Two functions in `src/curatedClasses.ts` are stubbed out --
`buildCatalogOptions` and `searchCuratedClasses` -- each currently just
`throw`s `not implemented`. Each has a JSDoc comment directly above it
describing its contract: what it takes in, what it must return, and the
correctness properties a real implementation needs to satisfy (in
particular, around resolving a class's identity correctly even when the
class was recently renumbered). Implement both functions for real.

Make

```sh
npm test
```

pass (all tests in `test/curatedClasses.test.ts`). Do not edit the test
file to make it pass -- implement the functions. If your chosen design
changes the shape of the data or functions, you may need to adapt the
fixtures or tests to match, but the underlying assertions (a renumbered
class is findable and displayable under its real, current number) should
still hold.

## Logging AI prompts

If you use an AI tool (Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT, etc.) while working on
this, keep a running log of what you asked it -- a text file, a chat
export, whatever's convenient. You'll walk through it in the review.
